ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the vertical axis is labeled Speed, and the horizontal axis is labeled Torque. Several labeled curves roughly start from near the same operating point: A rises steeply toward the upper right; B descends slowly toward the lower right, approximately in a straight line; C descends toward the lower right with a relatively obvious curve; D is a nearly vertical line segment. Then reason: The condition of the problem is that a DC series motor is overloaded under the rated power supply voltage, and the magnetic circuit has already saturated. When the magnetic circuit is saturated, the magnetic flux phi can approximately be regarded as a constant. For a DC motor, there are V = E + I_a R_a, E = k phi omega, T = k phi I_a. Because phi is approximately constant, I_a and T are approximately proportional; substituting gives omega = V/(k phi) - (R_a/(k^2 phi^2)) T. That is to say, under the rated voltage, as the torque increases, the armature resistance voltage drop increases, and the speed approximately decreases along a straight line with negative slope. In the figure, the torque-speed characteristic that conforms to “slowly decreasing, approximately linear” is the curve labeled B.

raw_record.question_text: In the below figure, which labeled curve approximately represents the torque-speed characteristic of a DC series motor fed from rated supply voltage when it is overloaded and its magnetic circuit is saturated?

method.method_draft: Use the text condition that the DC series motor is overloaded and magnetically saturated. Treat flux as nearly constant. Combine the DC motor equations to conclude that, at rated supply voltage, speed falls approximately linearly with increasing torque due to armature resistance voltage drop. In the figure, the curve with this shallow negative, almost linear speed-torque slope is labeled B, so select Curve B.

先描述图像：图中纵轴标为 Speed，横轴标为 Torque。几条标号曲线大致从同一工作点附近发出：A 向右上方陡升；B 向右下方缓慢、近似直线下降；C 向右下方较明显弯曲下降；D 是接近竖直的线段。
再推理：题目条件是直流串励电动机在额定电源电压下过载，并且磁路已饱和。磁路饱和时，磁通 phi 可近似看作常数。直流电机有 V = E + I_a R_a，E = k phi omega，T = k phi I_a。因为 phi 近似恒定，所以 I_a 与 T 近似成正比；代入得 omega = V/(k phi) - (R_a/(k^2 phi^2)) T。也就是说，在额定电压下，随着转矩增加，电枢电阻压降增大，速度近似按一条负斜率直线下降。图中符合“缓慢下降、近似线性”的转矩-速度特性的是标号 B 的曲线。

planner_metadata.image_role: Read the axes as speed on the vertical axis and torque on the horizontal axis. Identify the labeled shapes: A rises with torque, B is a gently downward-sloping nearly straight curve, C is a more sharply falling nonlinear curve, and D is nearly vertical.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question statement to know the machine is a DC series motor, supplied at rated voltage, under overload, and with saturated magnetic circuit.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: For a DC motor, V = E + IaRa and E = kφω, while T = kφIa. In magnetic saturation, φ is approximately constant even though the motor is a series motor. Therefore T is approximately proportional to armature current, and speed ω = (V - IaRa)/(kφ) decreases approximately linearly as torque/current increases.

method.method_draft: First identify what an ordinary unsaturated series motor would look like: a steeply decreasing inverse-type speed-torque curve, corresponding visually to curve C. Then apply the text’s special condition that the overloaded magnetic circuit is saturated, so the flux is almost fixed and the characteristic should no longer be the steep series-motor curve. Among the remaining labeled curves, the physically plausible saturated overload characteristic is the flatter downward curve B; A has the wrong positive slope and D would imply nearly constant torque. Therefore choose Curve B.

planner_metadata.image_role: Read the plotted alternatives by their qualitative shapes. Curve C is the steep inverse-like falling curve, curve B is the flatter falling curve, curve A increases with torque, and curve D is vertical at roughly constant torque.

planner_metadata.knowledge_role: An unsaturated DC series motor has φ roughly proportional to current, so torque grows roughly as Ia^2 and speed varies inversely with flux/current, producing a strongly nonlinear falling characteristic. Under overload saturation, flux no longer increases much with current, so the curve changes to a flatter constant-flux motor characteristic with only resistance-drop speed reduction.
